primary.thesis: As of 2026-07-25, CXMT (ChangXin Memory, China's leading DRAM maker) has filed for a STAR Market listing that would raise about 29.5B yuan. It is the largest domestic chip IPO in the pipeline and a policy priority. The listing sits inside a DRAM price supercycle, which should flip CXMT to large profits in 2026. In my view the IPO gets through registration and lists before year-end. STAR semiconductor debuts in 2025-26, such as Moore Threads and MetaX, closed their first day several hundred percent above the offer price. CXMT's float will be much larger, so its first-day pop should be smaller, perhaps 100-250% on an offer valuation in the few-hundred-billion-yuan range. That puts the first-day closing market cap, counted on all outstanding shares, most likely between 1T and 2T yuan. It clears the 1T rung but stops short of the 2T+ rungs, which would need a SK Hynix-style valuation on day one.

basket.reason: The IPO happens in 2026 and gets a supercycle valuation plus the usual STAR first-day premium, so full-share market cap reaches 1T yuan or more.
A large float and a big share count limit the first-day percentage gain. Reaching 2T would mean a valuation close to global memory peers on day one.
3T yuan (about $420B) would put CXMT above most global memory incumbents on its first day, which is too high.
3.5T is further out along the same logic: a cap that high would be larger than the whole STAR semiconductor sector's usual scale.

failure_narrative: The basket can lose in two ways. (a) Downside: the CSRC slows the pace of listings, registration drags on, or CXMT holds the IPO back to wait for fuller profit disclosure, so it does not list by 2026-12-31. It could also list with a weak first day after memory prices turn, closing below 1T. Either way C6 loses. (b) Upside: A-share speculative mania meets DRAM contract prices that are still rising. Retail demand and 'national champion' buying push the first-day close to 200-300%+ above an offer valuation of about 500B+, so the full-share market cap goes above 2T and the NO legs on C2 (and maybe C3) lose. I think the upside route is the more likely one, because 2026 profit estimates could justify SK Hynix-like multiples.
hedge_thesis: The global memory-equity boom keeps going and speeds up. Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron make new highs as HBM and commodity DRAM contract prices keep climbing into the second half of 2026, and Korean and US memory stocks re-rate. The mechanism is that A-share investors price CXMT off its listed global peers and off the DRAM price trend. The world where CXMT closes day one above 2T is the world where peer multiples and DRAM prices are strongest. So long exposure to overseas memory names and the KOSPI tends to pay off in the worlds where my upside-capped basket fails. The downside failure (a delay) mostly comes from Chinese regulatory timing and is less related to this. Still, a memory-price rollover that hurts CXMT's valuation would hit these peers too, so they only partly offset that case.
